content.comment_body: Good morning, I am wondering if it is possible to create buttons instead of switches in [product_name] Web Editor.

Hello [user_name], First, welcome to the forum. Since there are many languages, English is the chosen language here for international participation. Please write future posts in English. As for your question, it is not possible to change a digital value from a switch to a button directly in the Web Editor. This needs to be managed within your [product_name] program. Which variable are you using—a flag or a bit from the VM area?
I've attached a screenshot showing potential solutions to your issue.

Hello, I tried implementing solution 2, but it doesn't seem to work in KOP. In the online test image, you can still see the input linked to the switch is active. Why is this happening if both programs (KOP and FUP) should be equivalent? Thank you in advance.
Solution 2 functions in both FBD (FUP) and LAD (KOP). For the LAD (KOP) implementation, check the attached screen video.

Thank you! I was confused because in the FBD visualization, output Q1 is active while NI1 is off, as expected for an input maintained for just one scan cycle. In KOP, NI1 remains active, as if it wasn't reset after the scan. Is this just a graphical representation detail in [product_name] Soft?
In my view, LAD provides a misleading indication of NI1's status. LAD within [product_name] software tends to have bugs and lacks some options found in FBD.
Yes, it appears to be the case. Removing the RS block means input NI1 won't activate output Q1, so NI1 is actually reset after the first scan. Thanks a lot!

analysis.insight_summary: Participants highlighted that button-like behavior cannot be created directly in [product_name] Web Editor—only switches are available by default. Various programmatic workarounds within [product_name] were discussed. Users noted confusing and potentially misleading visual representations in the LAD (KOP) mode compared to FBD (FUP) in [product_name] Soft Comfort, raising questions about how accurately these modes reflect real statuses.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect digital inputs to be easily set as push-buttons instead of switches in the [product_name] Web Editor, and for the program logic visualizations to correctly show real-time statuses in all programming languages.
